applied.quote: At ModernWallet, we took each waiting period from the agency's own handbook, selling guide or regulation.
applied.replacement: At The Modern Wallet, we took each waiting period from the agency's own handbook, selling guide or regulation.
applied.why: Site self-description names the site The Modern Wallet, not ModernWallet.

applied.quote: Each agency counts to a different end date.
applied.replacement: FHA, VA and USDA count to different end dates.
applied.why: SOURCE gives end dates only for FHA, VA and USDA, not Fannie or Freddie.

applied.quote: The request starts with the trustee.
applied.why: SOURCE says consult the trustee; FHA wants court permission. No stated starting step.

applied.quote: That trustee-only route can leave an FHA file short, because HUD's handbook wording asks for permission from the bankruptcy court.
applied.replacement: HUD's FHA handbook wording asks for written permission from the bankruptcy court and does not mention the trustee.
applied.why: SOURCE states only the handbook wording, not this consequence for FHA files.

applied.quote: Fannie Mae names a divorce decree as supporting paperwork, so the same divorce can carry different weight depending on the loan.
applied.replacement: Fannie Mae names a divorce decree as an example of supporting paperwork.
applied.why: SOURCE lists the divorce decree as an example document only. It draws no weighting conclusion.

applied.quote: Meeting the waiting period gets a file considered, and underwriters then look for re-established credit and proof the cause will not repeat.
applied.replacement: Beyond the waiting period, underwriters look for re-established credit.
applied.why: No general underwriting sequence stated; non-recurrence proof is FHA-only.

applied.quote: These options do not fit a Chapter 7 discharged less than 12 months ago.
applied.replacement: A Chapter 7 discharged less than 12 months ago falls short of the FHA, VA and conventional rules.
applied.why: USDA sets no bar under 12 months, and VA says only generally not possible.

applied.quote: A Chapter 13 that ends in dismissal pushes conventional loans out to four years from the dismissal date, which can make FHA, VA or USDA the faster route.
applied.replacement: A Chapter 13 that ends in dismissal pushes conventional loans out to four years from the dismissal date, or two with documented extenuating circumstances.
applied.why: SOURCE gives no FHA/VA/USDA rule after a Chapter 13 dismissal.

applied.quote: Waiting periods to buy a house after Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy for government-backed and conventional loans, and what lenders check after discharge.
applied.replacement: Waiting periods to buy a house after Chapter 7 or Chapter 13 bankruptcy for FHA, VA, USDA and conventional loans, and what lenders check after discharge.
applied.why: SOURCE never calls FHA, VA or USDA loans 'government-backed'.

applied.quote: FHA, VA and USDA rules allow a home loan during a Chapter 13 plan once 12 months of on-time plan payments are made and the new debt is approved.
applied.replacement: Under FHA, VA and USDA rules, a home loan can be possible during a Chapter 13 plan once 12 months of on-time plan payments are made and the new debt is approved.
applied.why: SOURCE says these programs do not disqualify or may favorably consider. It does not say they allow the loan.

applied.quote:
Fannie Mae gives these as examples of supporting documents:

- A divorce decree
- Medical reports or bills
- A notice of job layoff
- Job severance papers

The agencies do not count the same events.
applied.why: SOURCE gives no comparison of which events each agency counts.

applied.quote: Request Loan Estimates from several lenders, since every lender uses the same standard form.
applied.replacement: Request Loan Estimates from several lenders so you can compare them. Every lender uses the same standard form.
applied.why: SOURCE states both facts but never links them as cause and reason.
